verses.sanskrit:
सौतिरुवाच।
              एतच्छ्रुत्वा जरत्कारुर्भृशं शोकपरायणः। उवाच तान्पितॄन्दुःखाद्बाष्पसंदिग्धया गिरा॥१॥
verses.english: Sauti said: Having heard all this, Jaratkaru became exceedingly sorry. He spoke to the pitres in sorrow and his words were choked by tears.

verses.sanskrit:
जरत्कारुरुवाच।
              मम पूर्वे भवन्तो वै पितरः सपितामहाः। तद्ब्रूत यन्मया कार्यं भवतां प्रियकाम्यया॥२॥
verses.english: Jaratkaru said: You are my sires and grand-sires. I am that very Jaratkaru. Tell me what I should do.

verses.sanskrit: अहमेव जरत्कारुः किल्बिषी भवतां सुतः। ते दण्डं धारयत मे दुष्कृतेरकृतात्मनः॥३॥
verses.english: I am that Jaratkaru, your sinful son. I am a worthless man, a man of sinful deeds. Pray, punish me.

verses.sanskrit:
पितर ऊचुः।
              पुत्र दिष्ट्याऽसि संप्राप्त इमं देशं यदृच्छया। किमर्थं च त्वया ब्रह्मन्नकृतो दारसङ्ग्रहः॥४॥
verses.english: O son, you have come by good luck at this spot in your travel. O Brahmana, why have you not taken a wife?

verses.sanskrit:
जरत्कारुरुवाच।
              ममायं पितरो नित्यं हृद्यर्थः परिवर्तते। ऊर्ध्वरेताः शरीरं वै प्रापयेयममुत्र वै॥५॥
verses.english: Jaratkaru said: O Pitris, I have this desire always in my heart, that having kept my sexual passion under complete control, I shall take this body to the other world.

verses.sanskrit: न दारान्वै करिष्येऽहमिति मे भावितं मनः। एवं दृष्ट्वा तु भवतः शकुन्तानिव लम्बतः॥६॥
verses.english: My mind is possessed with the idea that I must not take a wife. But having seen you, my sires, hanging like birds.

verses.sanskrit: मया निवर्तिता बुद्धिर्ब्रह्मचर्यात्पितामहाः। करिष्ये वः प्रियं कामं निवेक्ष्येऽहमसंशयम्॥७॥
verses.english: O grandfathers, my mind has been diverted from Brahmacharya, I shall certainly do your favourite work.

verses.sanskrit: सनाम्नीं यद्यहं कन्यामुपलप्स्ये कदाचन। भविष्यति च या काचिद्भैक्ष्यवत्स्वयमुद्यता॥८॥
verses.english: (I shall certainly marry), if I get a bride of my own name, who will bestow herself on me of her own accord, who will come to me as a gift and whom I shall not have to maintain.

verses.sanskrit: प्रतिग्रहीता तामस्मि न भरेयं च यामहम्। एवं विधमहं कुर्यां निवेशं प्राप्नुयां यदि। अन्यथा न करिष्येऽहं सत्यमेतत्पितामहाः॥९॥
तत्र चोत्पत्स्यते जन्तुर्भवतां तारणाय वै। शाश्वताश्चाव्ययाश्चैव तिष्ठन्तु पितरो मम॥१०॥
verses.english: Otherwise I shall not marry. O grandsires, I speak to you the truth. The offspring that will be begotten on her shall be the means of your salvation and O my fathers, you will then live for ever in blessed happiness and without the apprehension of a fall.

verses.sanskrit:
सौतिरुवाच।
              एवमुक्त्वा तु स पितॄंश्चचार पृथिवी मुनिः। न च स्म लभते भार्यां वृद्धोऽयमिति शानक॥११॥
verses.english: Sauti said : The Rishi (Jaratkaru), having said all this to the ancestors, (left the place and) roamed over the world again. O Shaunaka, although he grew old, he did not get a wife.

verses.sanskrit: यदा निर्वेदमापन्नः पितृभिश्चोदिस्तथा। तदाऽरण्यं स गत्वोच्चैश्चुक्रोश भृशदुःखितः॥१२॥
verses.english: He was very sorry that he was not successful, but directed by his ancestors he continued the search. He went into the forest and shouted aloud in grief.

verses.sanskrit: सत्वरण्यगतः प्राज्ञः पितॄणां हितकाम्यया। उवाच कन्यां याचामि तिस्रो वाचः शनैरिमाः॥१३॥
verses.english: Having gone into the forest, the wise Rishi, moved by the desire of doing good to his ancestors, said, “I shall ask for a bride, distinctly uttering the words thrice.

verses.sanskrit: यानि भूतानि सन्तीह स्थावराणि चराणि च। अन्तर्हितानि वा यानि तानि शृण्वन्तु मे वचः॥१४॥
verses.english: Whatever creatures are, mobile immobile, visible of invisible, O you all, hear or my words.

verses.sanskrit: उग्रे तपसि वर्तन्तं पितरश्चोदयन्ति माम्। निविशस्वेति दुःखार्ताः सन्तानस्य चिकीर्षया॥१५॥
verses.english: I am a man, engaged in severe penances, but my ancestors, afflicted with grief, have told me, "Get yourself married to beget a son."

verses.sanskrit: निवेशायाखिलां भूमिं कन्याभैक्ष्यं चरामि भोः। दरिद्रो दुःखशीलश्च पितृभिः सन्नियोजितः॥१६॥
verses.english: Directed by my ancestors, I'm roaming in poverty and sorrow all over the world for wedding a maiden whom I shall get as a gift.

verses.sanskrit: यस्य कन्याऽस्ति भूतस्य ये मयेह प्रकीर्तिताः। ते मे कन्यां प्रयच्छन्तु चरतः सर्वतोदिशम्॥१७॥
verses.english: Let any of those creatures, whom I (now) address, if he has a daughter, bestow her on me who am roving all over the world for a bride.

verses.sanskrit: मम कन्या सनाम्नीया भैक्ष्यवच्चोदिता भवेत्। भरेयं चैव यां नाहं तां मे कन्यां प्रयच्छत॥१८॥
verses.english: A bride, who bears the same name with me, who will be given to me as a gift and whom I shall not have to maintain,(If there is such a bride), O bestow her on me.

verses.sanskrit: ततस्ते पन्नगा ये वै जरत्कारौ समाहिताः। तामादाय प्रवृत्तिं ते वासुकेः प्रत्यवेदयन्॥१९॥
verses.english: Thereupon those snakes, who had been appointed to watch Jaratkaru, knowing his intention, gave information to Vasuki.

verses.sanskrit: तेषां श्रुत्वा स नागेन्द्रस्तां कन्यां समलङ्कृताम्। प्रगृह्यारण्यमगमत्समीपं तस्य पन्नगः॥२०॥
verses.english: The king of the snakes immediately went to the place where the Rishi was, taking with him his sister, decked with various ornaments.

verses.sanskrit: तत्र तां भैक्ष्यवत्कन्यां प्रादात्तस्मै महात्मने। नागेन्द्रो वासुकिर्ब्रह्मन्न स तां प्रत्यगृह्णत॥२१॥
verses.english: O Brahmana, the king of the snakes Vasuki, having gone there, offered the maiden as a gift to that high-souled Rishi. But he did not at once accept her.

verses.sanskrit: असनामेति वै मत्वा भरणे चाविचारिते। मोक्षभावे स्थितश्चापि मन्दीभूतः परिग्रहे॥२२॥
verses.english: The Rishi, thinking her not to be of the same name with himself and seeing also that the question of her maintenance was not settled, reflected for a while and hesitated to accept her.

verses.sanskrit: ततो नाम स कन्यायाः पप्रच्छ भृगुनन्दन। वासुकिं भरणं चास्या न कुर्यामित्युवाच ह॥२३॥
verses.english: O descendant of Bhrigu, he then asked Vasuki the name of the maiden and he told him also, “I shall not maintain her."
verses.bhavadeepa: असनामेति मोक्षे स्थितस्य परिग्रहो दुःखायेति पितृप्रयोजनमात्रं कार्यमित्याशयः ॥२२॥
